JUDGMENT
This claim petition is filed under Sec.166 of M.V Act, 1988 seeking compensation for the death caused in a Road Traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioners in the nutshell is that on 28.08.2023 at about 4.30 to 4.40 p.m the deceased was driving the Toyota Qualis car bearing Reg.No.KA-01-MF-8055 from Male Mahadeshwara Hill towards Bengaluru Side, on Kanakapura - Malavalli road and when he reached near Kemmale Gate, NH-948 road, Malavalli Kanakapura road, Sathanoor Hobli, Kanakapura Taluk, Ramanagara District, at that point of time the driver of KSRTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA- 42-F-1745 has driven from Kanakapura side towards Malavalli side, opposite direction with high speed, driven on extreme right side road in a rash and negligent manner so as to endangering to human life and dashed against the deceased driving Toyota car, and dragged the car at a distance of 50 to 75 feet from the accident spot towards the car side road, in which the car was proceeding on correct side and caused the accident.
Due to the terrific impact the deceased sustained grievous injuries all over his body and was succumbed to the fatal injuries on spot.
Postmortem was conducted and corpse was handed over to the family members, who conducted funeral and other ceremonies by spending substantial amount.

It is alleged that the deceased was working as Section officer at Karnataka Legislative Assembly, Secretariat, Vidhanasoudha, Bengaluru and earning Rs.85,000/- p.m. and because of untimely death of deceased, the petitioners have suffered economically as well as emotionally.

After thorough investigation, the jurisdictional police have filed charge sheet against drivers of KSRTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-42-F-1745 and Qualis car bearing Reg.No.KA-01-MF-8055 i.e., deceased and the accident in issue is occurred due to negligent driving of the aforesaid vehicle drivers.
The respondent being the RC owner of KSRTC bus is liable to pay compensation.
3. The respondent / KSRTC Transport Corporation contended that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts and same is liable to be dismissed.
Further the petition is bad for non joinder of necessary parties.
It is alleged that the accident is occured due to the sole negligence of the driver of Qualis car / deceased.
The respondent corporation was no way responsible for the occurrence of accident.
This respondent denied the rash and negligent act of the driver of its bus driver.
On the contrary it is stated that on the date and time of alleged accident the bus in question was on its schedule trip from Kanakapura to Halaguru.

The driver of the KSRTC bus drive the same in slowly and cautiously on the extreme left side of the road by observing all the traffic rules and regulations and while so proceeding on Kanakapura - Halaguru Main road, near Kemmale Gate at that point of time the deceased driving the Qualis car bearing Reg.No.KA-01-MF-8055 he came from the opposite side in a rash and negligent manner with terrific speed in a zig-zag manner,

sentences.text: observing the same the bus driver sensing some mishap, slowed down the speed of the bus and taken to its left side and when the things stood thus, car just like a bolt from the blue, came to its extreme right side of the road, by crossing the midpoint, the driver of the bus, that too to extreme his right edge of the road, to avoid being hit by the car swear the bus to the little bit right side, but inspite of the same the driver of the car / deceased, due to the over speed and as the car moving in a zig zag manner totally lost control over the him and dashed violently against the bus and caused the accident, and due to the terrific hit by the car the bus moved to the right side.
As such, for the alleged accident the driver of the Qualis car / deceased was wholly and solely responsible, but the driver of bus in question was no way responsible.
However the petitioners with an oblique reasons foisted a false case in active collusion with the policy by creating a false crime records against this respondent driver.
Rest of the averments of the petition are repudiated as false and baseless and it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

4. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues were framed :
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioners proves that they are the legal heirs and dependents of the deceased ?
2) Whether the petitioners prove that the deceased succumbed to the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident that occurred on 28.08.2023 at about 4.30 to 4.40 p.m., near Kemmale gate, NH- 948 road, Malavalli-Kanakapura road, Sathanoor Hobli, Kanakapura Taluk, Ramanagara District,
due to actionable negligence of the drivers of KSRTC bus bearing No.KA-42-F-1745 and Toyota car bearing Reg.No.KA-01-MF-8055 ?

3) Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation as prayed? If so, at what rate and from whom ?
4) What order or award ?
5. The Petitioner No.1 examined herself as PW.1.
Ex's.P1 to 19 were marked on behalf of the petitioners.
The petitioners have also examined the eye-witness to the accident as PW.2 and through her Ex.P.20 was marked.
The employer of the deceased was examined as PW.3, through her Ex.P.21 and 22 got marked.

The driver of KSRTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-42-F- 1745 was examined as RW.1 and got marked Ex.R.1.
6.
Heard both counsels for the petitioners and respondent on merits.
Perused the entire materials placed on record.

REASONS 8. ISSUE No.1:
The petitioners claim that, petitioner No.1 is the wife and petitioner No.2 & 3 are the children and petitioner No.4 is the mother of the deceased.
To prove the same, petitioner No.1 filed affidavit-in-lieu of her chief- examination and deposed about the above relationship.
The Aadhaar cards of petitioners and deceased at Ex.P.11 to 15 and contents of the police papers do fortify the said fact.
It is pertinent to note that, this relationship of the petitioners with the deceased was not disputed by the respondents.

Since the evidence led by the petitioners is satisfactory and also taking into consideration the fact that there are no rival claimants, this Tribunal hold that the petitioners are the legal representatives of the deceased.
Therefore, petitioners are the legal heirs and dependents of deceased.
Hence, this Tribunal answers to issue No.1 In the Affirmative.
9. ISSUE No.2:

The evidence on record reveals that after the receipt of the complaint, the jurisdictional police registered a FIR against the deceased / driver of car bearing Reg.No.KA- 01-MF-8055 and took up investigation.
During the course of investigation material evidence connected to the accident was collected by them.
There is no dispute regarding the occurrence of the accident on the relevant date, time and place.
The death of the deceased person due to the injuries sustained in the Road Traffic Accident is also not in conflict.
The only issue with which the parties are at loggerheads is with regard to the factum of negligence.

The question as to who was responsible for the accident has to be answered by looking into the evidence on record, perusal of which makes it evident that the deceased was driving the Qualis car bearing Reg.No.KA-01-MF-8055 in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the front left side of the KSRTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-42-F-1745, as a result of which the deceased and other inmates of the car succumbed on the spot.
This goes to show that the deceased / driver of the Qualis car had failed to adhere to the basic traffic rules & regulations and acted in a gross negligent manner.
10. The other tortfeasor i.e., driver of the KSRTC bearing Reg.No.KA-42-F-1745 (RW.1) who vehemently asserted that the said bus was express bus from Kanakapura to Halaguru.
He stated that the said road is NH-948 and the said road is straight road.
He further admitted that at the time of driving the vehicles were came opposite side could have been seen, he had seen the qualis car from 10 feet distance.
He further admitted that their was express bus, therefore there was a schedule to reach the destination.
The width of the road is 20 feet and accident took place at 4.30 p.m.

The learned counsel for petitioners put some questions to the driver of the KSRTC bus (RW.1) as :
"Question : Why you had taken the bus on right side on the road ?
Answer : The driver of the car came opposite side in zig zag manner, he came on left side of the road i.e on my side, so I had taken the bus on right side to avoid the accident".
RW.1 further admitted that the left front portion was damaged and has not produced photo of damaged bus.

He stated that he has not given any complaint as accident took place due to the Geethamma Y Alias Geetha Y vs K.S.R.T.C on 3 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50156719/
4 negligence of the deceased, because he was also injured.

He stated that after 4 days from the date of accident he had taken bail from jurisdictional police and the criminal case is still pending at JMFC,
Kanakapura.
These elicitation make it amply clear that as RW.1 was driving his bus at a high speed and in a rash manner and bus dragged the car for certain distance.

A case of accident that would lead to grievous injuries at the maximum, unfortunately has lead to death due to the careless act of RW.1.
11.
Smt. Bhagyalakshmi.
S (PW.2) filed affidavit evidence stating that she had eye-witnessed the accident.
She stated that she was traveling as passenger in an offending vehicle KSRTC Bus bearing No.KA-42-F-1745 from Kanakapura towards Halagur side.
The driver of the offending bus has driven with high speed and dashed against the Toyota car and after dragged the car at a distance of 50-75 feet from the accident spot.
The driver of the car was proceeding on correct side road and on proper lane from the opposite direction to an offending vehicle KSRTC bus.
During the course of her cross-examination, she admitted that she was sitting beside the driver seat on first seat.
She admitted that the road was busy road and the accident took place near the Kennare Gate.
She admitted that the bus which was proceeding at left side on the road, suddenly came towards right side and dashed to the car which was proceeding opposite to the bus on the left side.
She stated that if the bus driver had been drove the vehicle at his side, accident could have been avoided.
Nothing significant could be extracted from PW.2's mouth to disbelieve her presence at the spot of the accident, at the time of its occurrence.
12. Further on perusal of complaint given by one Shivalingegowda he being complainant witness in charge sheet.

He stated that on 28.08.2023 at about 4.30 to 4.40 p.m, one green Coloured Qualis car was coming from Halagur side with high speed in a zig zag manner and at the same time one KSRTC bus which was coming from Kanakapura side with high speed in rash and negligent manner and both have coming with high speed and themselves have caused the accident on head on collision.
He is third person.
He cannot be suspected that he is telling lie.
The complaint lodged by Shivalingegowda clearly shows that there was gross negligence of drivers of both vehicles.
As per the contents there was more negligence of driver of Qualis car / deceased.
From the testimonies of PW's.1 & 2 and complainant it is clear that the accident occurred due to the rash & negligent driving of the both drivers.

Based on FIS, the jurisdictional police registered FIR as per Ex.P.1, investigated the matter and laid charge sheet (Ex.P.8) against the drivers of KSRTC bearing Reg.No.KA-42-F-1745 and deceased / Qualis car bearing Reg.No.KA-01-MF-8055 for the offences punishable u/s's 279, 337, 338 and 304(A) of IPC.
This Court is aware of the fact that charge sheet is not a conclusive proof to come to conclusion with regard to rash and negligent act.
But having regard to the Ex.P.3 & 4 which was read in consonance with the Ex.P.8 Charge sheet it is crystal clear that there is an rash and negligent act of the drivers of both car & KSRTC bus.

If driver of car /
deceased had driven his car in his side and in normal speed, the accident could have been avoided.
Accordingly if KSRTC bus driver was driving the bus in normal speed also it could have been avoided.
13. Thus the unchallenged final report filed by the police clearly establishes negligence on the part of the drivers of the car and KSRTC bus.

A case of accident that would lead to grievous injuries at the maximum, unfortunately has lead to injuries caused to the deceased due to the careless act of Geethamma Y Alias Geetha Y vs K.S.R.T.C on 3 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50156719/

sentences.text: The self serving statement of the driver of the KSRTC bus cannot be attached any evidentiary value as he would obviously give a different version of the accident to escape from the criminal liability which would in turn affect his employment prospects.

Be that as it may the inference that can be drawn from the police documents and evidence of PW.1 is that the driver of car and the driver of KSRTC bus were responsible for the occurrence of the accident.
Thereby the negligence attributed towards driver of car / deceased and driver of KSRTC bus in the ratio of 70 : 30.

With this observation Issue No.2 is answered as 'In the Affirmative'.
14. ISSUE NO.3 : LOSS OF DEPENDENCY INCLUDING FUTURE PROSPECTS:

The petitioners have produced the Driving Licence, Aadhar card and Service Register to show the age of the deceased as per Ex.P10, Ex.P.15 and Ex.P.21 wherein the date of birth of deceased is shown as 10.01.1974, which indicates that he was aged (49 years 7 months 18 days) 50 years on the date of accident.

Therefore the appropriate multiplier as per Sarla Verma's case for the said age group is '13'.
15.

In order to substantiate the fact the deceased was working as a Section officer at Karnataka Legislative Assembly, Secretariat, Vidhanasoudha, Bengaluru and earning Rs.85,000/- p.m, the petitioners have produced ID card and Pay slips at Ex.P.16 and 19 and also got examined the Secretary of Karnataka Vidhanasoudha Secretariat, Bengaluru as PW.3.
This witness produced the certified copy of Service Register and 6-pay slips of the deceased, which is exhibited at ExP.21 & 22.

On perusal of Ex.P.22 pay slips it discloses that the PW.3 has produced March-2023, April-2023,
July and August-2023 pay slips.
Other two payslips are pertaining to one Kotresh. S.M and they were not belongs to deceased.
Further on perusal of pay slips produced by the petitioners for the months of March-2023 to August-2023.
The testimony of this witness which is fortified by the said exhibit was not displaced during cross-examination.
16. Generally it is the last drawn salary that needs to be taken into consideration for the calculation of compensation.

But in this case as the deceased succumbed to the injuries sustained in the road traffic accident that occurred on 28.08.2023, as per Ex.P.22 his income for August-2023 cannot be considered for determining compensation.
Further during August-2023, the deceased's pay was calculated for 31 days and in the said document they paid Rs.82,414/-.
The PW.3 also stated that the gross salary paid upto 28.08.2023 is Rs.74,453/- as he was working 28 days during that month.
Hence his salary for the last full worked month i.e., July-2023 is taken into account for computing the dependency compensation.
The gross salary of the deceased for the said month is Rs.82,414/-.
On careful perusal of the salary slips from April-2023 to August-2023 it depicts that he has paid Income Tax of Rs.4,000/- every month.
As such the gross salary of deceased is considered as Rs.82,414/-.

As per the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited v/s Pranay Sethi and others, except income tax no deduction is to be made from the salary of the deceased qua other allowances.

PW.3 stated that there is a provision for compensatory service of job.
They have submitted application for compensatory job but they have not submitted relevant documents.
Therefore it is under process.

sentences.text: Further the petitioners have also not produced the Form No.16 or Income Tax returns of deceased before this Tribunal to substantiate that how much Income tax they have paid.
Hence this tribunal taken Rs.4,000/- per month as Income tax and it comes Rs.48,000/- per annum.
17. Be that as it may, annual income works out to Rs.9,88,968/- (Rs.82,414 X 12).
Out of the said annual income, professional tax and income tax needs to be deducted.
The calculation table for which stands as follows :
Annual Gross Salary 9,88,968  (Rs.82,414 x12)

Annual Professional Tax (less) 2,400  Total 9,86,568  Less Tax Exemption 2,50,000  (for the year 2023)
 Taxable Income 7,36,568

Tax payable @ 5% on 48,000  Rs.9,86,568/- (during the year  2023)
 Gross Income 9,88,968  Less Total Tax payable 50,400  (2,400 + 48,000 =12,086)
 Annual Established Income 9,38,568  Monthly Established Income 78,214  (9,38,568 / 12)
18.
In the case on hand the deceased was aged 50 years.
His income is taken as Rs.78,214/- p.m.
In this case the deceased being an employee of the State Government had a permanent job.
Therefore as per dictum of Hon'ble Apex Court in AIR 2017 SC 5157, 30% of income is to be added towards future prospects.
30% of Rs.78,214/- works out to Rs.23,464/-.
Therefore the total income comes to Rs.1,01,678/- (78,214 + 23,464).
There are four dependents.
Hence 1/4 th is to be deducted towards his personal expenses.
1/4th of Rs.1,01,678/- works out to Rs.25,420/-.
Income for consideration is Rs.76,258/- (1,01,678 - 25,420).
Annual income works out to Rs.9,15,096/- (76,258 X 12).
Appropriate multiplier is '13'.

Thus loss of dependency works out to Rs.1,18,96,248/- (Rs.9,15,096 X 13) which is rounded off to Rs.1,18,96,300/-.
19.

Further, as Law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others, the compensation towards loss to estate, funeral expenses and consortium is to be awarded.

20. In this case, the petitioner No.2 & 3 are the children and the petitioner No.4 is the mother of the deceased

and as per the decision reported in (2018) 12 SCC 130 in the case of Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and others, the petitioner No.2 to 4 are entitled for filial consortium, as the filial consortium is the right of the parents and children to get compensation in the case of an accidental death of a children and father as the case may be.

REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY : Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% per annum is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
23. Admittedly it is a case of composite negligence where injuries / death has been caused by a combined wrongful act of joint tortfeasors.

Under such circumstances, each wrong doer i.e., the respondent and deceased herein and the respondent corporation is liable and accordingly directed to pay the aforesaid award amount to the claimants together with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.

The Respondent being the RC owner/insurer of the KSRTC bus bearing No.KA-42-F-1745 is liable and directed to pay the compensation amount with interest in the ratio of 30%, within two months from the date of this order.
As such, this issue is answered accordingly.
Hence issue No.3 is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.

ISSUE NO.4 :

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.36,30,284/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire award amount.
The respondent is liable to pay and directed to deposit the aforesaid amount together with interest within a period of one month from the date of award.

On deposit of the award amount together with interest, the claimants are entitled for the compensation amount by way of apportionment as follows :
Petitioner No.1 - 50% Petitioner No.2 - 15% Petitioner No.3 - 15% Petitioner No.4 - 20%

Out of the share amount of Petitioners No.1 & 2 a sum equal to 25% shall be deposited in their names in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of their choice for a period of 3 years and the remaining 75% shall be released to them through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
However the said petitioners No.1 & 2 are at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on their deposit amount from time to time.

The share amount apportioned in the name of minor petitioner No.3 is ordered to be deposited in his name vide Fixed Deposit till he attains the age of majority, at any Nationalized/ Scheduled Bank as per the choice of the next friend/Natural guardian of the said minor petitioner.
The entire share amount apportioned in the name of petitioner No.4 shall be released to in her favour through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw an award accordingly.

opennyai_summary.facts:
This claim petition is filed under Sec.166 of M.V Act, 1988 seeking compensation for the death caused in a Road Traffic accident.
Due to the terrific impact the deceased sustained grievous injuries all over his body and was succumbed to the fatal injuries on spot.
Postmortem was conducted and corpse was handed over to the family members, who conducted funeral and other ceremonies by spending substantial amount.
After thorough investigation, the jurisdictional police have filed charge sheet against drivers of KSRTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-42-F-1745 and Qualis car bearing Reg.No.KA-01-MF-8055 i.e., deceased and the accident in issue is occurred due to negligent driving of the aforesaid vehicle drivers.
The respondent being the RC owner of KSRTC bus is liable to pay compensation.
opennyai_summary.issue:
4. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues were framed :
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioners proves that they are the legal heirs and dependents of the deceased ?
2) Whether the petitioners prove that the deceased succumbed to the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident that occurred on 28.08.2023 at about 4.30 to 4.40 p.m., near Kemmale gate, NH- 948 road, Malavalli-Kanakapura road, Sathanoor Hobli, Kanakapura Taluk, Ramanagara District,
due to actionable negligence of the drivers of KSRTC bus bearing No.KA-42-F-1745 and Toyota car bearing Reg.No.KA-01-MF-8055 ?
3) Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation as prayed? If so, at what rate and from whom ?
4) What order or award ?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Since the evidence led by the petitioners is satisfactory and also taking into consideration the fact that there are no rival claimants, this Tribunal hold that the petitioners are the legal representatives of the deceased.
Therefore, petitioners are the legal heirs and dependents of deceased.
The question as to who was responsible for the accident has to be answered by looking into the evidence on record, perusal of which makes it evident that the deceased was driving the Qualis car bearing Reg.No.KA-01-MF-8055 in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the front left side of the KSRTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-42-F-1745, as a result of which the deceased and other inmates of the car succumbed on the spot.
This goes to show that the deceased / driver of the Qualis car had failed to adhere to the basic traffic rules & regulations and acted in a gross negligent manner.
This Court is aware of the fact that charge sheet is not a conclusive proof to come to conclusion with regard to rash and negligent act.
But having regard to the Ex.P.3 & 4 which was read in consonance with the Ex.P.8 Charge sheet it is crystal clear that there is an rash and negligent act of the drivers of both car & KSRTC bus.
If driver of car /
deceased had driven his car in his side and in normal speed, the accident could have been avoided.
Accordingly if KSRTC bus driver was driving the bus in normal speed also it could have been avoided.
13. Thus the unchallenged final report filed by the police clearly establishes negligence on the part of the drivers of the car and KSRTC bus.
A case of accident that would lead to grievous injuries at the maximum, unfortunately has lead to injuries caused to the deceased due to the careless act of Geethamma Y Alias Geetha Y vs K.S.R.T.C on 3 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50156719/
5 drivers of both car and KSRTC bus.
The self serving statement of the driver of the KSRTC bus cannot be attached any evidentiary value as he would obviously give a different version of the accident to escape from the criminal liability which would in turn affect his employment prospects.
Thereby the negligence attributed towards driver of car / deceased and driver of KSRTC bus in the ratio of 70 : 30.
As such the gross salary of deceased is considered as Rs.82,414/-.
As per the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited v/s Pranay Sethi and others, except income tax no deduction is to be made from the salary of the deceased qua other allowances.
Even otherwise from the elicitation brought out during the course of cross-examination of PW.3 it is crystal clear at the time of death he was Senior Section Officer and further stated that the wife of deceased is entitled for pension.
50% of last pay is the pension to the wife of deceased.
and as per the decision reported in (2018) 12 SCC 130 in the case of Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and others, the petitioner No.2 to 4 are entitled for filial consortium, as the filial consortium is the right of the parents and children to get compensation in the case of an accidental death of a children and father as the case may be.
An accident leading to the death of a father cause great shock and agony to the children of the deceased and she lost her love and affection towards his/her father, as well as Petitioner no.4 towards deceased her son.
REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY : Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% per annum is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
23. Admittedly it is a case of composite negligence where injuries / death has been caused by a combined wrongful act of joint tortfeasors.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Therefore, petitioner No.2 to 4 are entitled for Rs.40,000/- each under the head of Filial consortium.
Under such circumstances, each wrong doer i.e., the respondent and deceased herein and the respondent corporation is liable and accordingly directed to pay the aforesaid award amount to the claimants together with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
The Respondent being the RC owner/insurer of the KSRTC bus bearing No.KA-42-F-1745 is liable and directed to pay the compensation amount with interest in the ratio of 30%, within two months from the date of this order.
As such, this issue is answered accordingly.
Hence issue No.3 is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.
Geethamma
ISSUE NO.4 :
In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.36,30,284/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire award amount.
The respondent is liable to pay and directed to deposit the aforesaid amount together with interest within a period of one month from the date of award.
On deposit of the award amount together with interest, the claimants are entitled for the compensation amount by way of apportionment as follows :
Petitioner No.1 - 50% Petitioner No.2 - 15% Petitioner No.3 - 15% Petitioner No.4 - 20%
Out of the share amount of Petitioners No.1 & 2 a sum equal to 25% shall be deposited in their names in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of their choice for a period of 3 years and the remaining 75% shall be released to them through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
However the said petitioners No.1 & 2 are at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on their deposit amount from time to time.
The share amount apportioned in the name of minor petitioner No.3 is ordered to be deposited in his name vide Fixed Deposit till he attains the age of majority, at any Nationalized/ Scheduled Bank as per the choice of the next friend/Natural guardian of the said minor petitioner.
The entire share amount apportioned in the name of petitioner No.4 shall be released to in her favour through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw an award accordingly.
